intro.title: 档案#59–Z(终幕): 钥匙议会

children.text: 取决于你如何到达此处……
你因状况报告(由于时间耗尽)到达此处
你自行前往通古斯卡

你在黑暗中醒来。头上的麻袋已经被取下，扔到一边。有人用力捏你的脸，打了你一两巴掌。“醒醒。”一个邪恶的声音命令道。你眨眨眼，恢复了意识，不无惊恐地意识到自己和同伴被人绑在了椅子上。嘴里塞了东西，你叫不出声，只能发出呜咽。

等到你的眼睛终于适应了昏暗的光线，你发觉自己肯定是在地下。这间巨大的厅堂没有窗子，石壁打磨光滑，由水银蒸汽灯略微照亮。墙上挂着猩红的织毯，还有几架玻璃柜子，里面装着古老的遗物和历史上的神器。一张巨大的桌子占据了房间中央，上面精巧地刻画着线条和圆环的纹样。桌旁围绕着一圈身影，有的你熟悉，有的并认不出。它们身上都有红色。你的心跳到了嗓子眼。“你被带到此处，清算你对同志会犯下的罪行。”那个声音宣言道，“如果议会同意，也可能会嘉奖你的功绩。我们将清点有谁将为你辩护，又有谁要指控你。”

进入审判。

要不是有泰勒专员的情报，你怕是永远也找不到红色同志会在这里的秘密藏身处。这栋建筑就在西伯利亚核心地带的地下。离此处不远有一个神秘的火山口，标记了著名的通古斯卡事件——那次爆炸，抑或是撞击？其中真相已经被掩埋在迷雾中超过十年了。也许这起诡异的事件还和同志会有着联系——不，自从你知道同志会拥有的危险神器，早就不怀疑这一点了。问题只是：是谁先来的？

大雪掩盖了遥远荒野的入口，但你最终还是找到了——雪丘上有一扇未加标记的铁门，从远处几乎不可能看到。你惊讶地发现门居然没锁……但你一进去，同志会的守卫就迎了上来。他们带着怀疑的眼神，穿着熟悉的红衣。“我们一直在等你。”其中一个狞笑着说道，“来吧，议会就要开始了。”

你别无选择，只能跟上。守卫领你一路往下，越走越深。狭窄的阶梯两旁石壁打磨得非常光滑，漫长的走道黑咕隆咚，十分单调。终于，你来到一间巨大的厅室，这里没有窗子，由水银蒸汽灯略微照亮。墙上挂着猩红的织毯，还有几架玻璃柜子，里面装着古老的遗物和历史上的神器。一张巨大的桌子占据了房间中央，上面精巧地刻画着线条和圆环的纹样。桌旁围绕着一圈身影，有的你熟悉，有的并认不出。它们身上都有红色。你背后的门猛地关上，你的心跳到了嗓子眼。“你来得正好。”同志会众人中传出一个声音，“我们刚要开始投票。”

你问这次投票是为了什么，嘴巴不由得发干。你总觉得来这里只是为了亲眼见证自己的毁灭。“这是一场召集的会议。清算你对同志会犯下的罪行。如果议会同意，也可能会嘉奖你的功绩。我们将清点有谁将为你辩护，又有谁要指控你。”你感到背后突然有人将你绑住，嘴里也塞了东西。“只是走个流程，我保证。”守卫奸笑着慢慢说道。

进入审判。

审判：同志会投票决定你的命运。

阅读下列每个部分的相关文本，按顺序记录所有的投票。每个“赞成”票表示该同志会成员想要看你去死。每个“反对”票表示该同志会成员想要护你周全。弃权票或沉默既非赞成也非反对。
[count]票
[count]票

如果特别小组援助了骑士：亚历山大年长的“骑士”迈步向前，吸引了房间里所有人的注意力。“我尊敬的同道啊。我们面前的几位，尽管……所忠非人……但确实值得我们的尊重和认可。要是没有他们的帮助，我们在亚历山大的圣堂就要陷落。我不得不说，还是陷落在自己人手里。我相信这已经足以彰显他们的价值。”其他几位点点头同意。聚集的会员环顾四周，但并没有人出来反驳。也许恶兽还在养伤。

暗红骑士投票“反对”。
深红斗篷的恶兽默认弃权。

如果特别小组未能阻挡恶兽：深红斗篷遮蔽下的恶兽发出隆隆的叫声。“血。”它的声明非常简单。这凶煞的声音吓得你退缩，脊背发颤。“必须要见血。”你环顾四周，寻找亚历山大年长的骑士，希望他能说服其他人冷静……但他不在这里。

暗红骑士默认弃权。
深红斗篷的恶兽投票“赞成”。

如果你和暗红骑士之间恩怨未了：“应该采取什么措施，一目了然。”来自亚历山大，仪表堂堂的年长“骑士”宣称道，“这些人不值得信任，还意图颠覆我们的控制。必须予以消灭。”在桌子另一端，骑士的敌人，深红长袍笼罩的阴影吼道：“我们终于有一次意见一致。”他隆隆的声音凶狠而粗野。骑士的眼睛眯了起来。“别自以为是了。”他警告道。

暗红骑士投票“赞成”。
深红斗篷的恶兽投票“赞成”。

如果大战打响：你和聚集起来的同志会成员环顾四周，寻找亚历山大的两位代表，但得到的只有一片寂静。“看来我们中有两位决定不出席了。”同志会中的一员声明道。你不禁好奇他们是否还活着。兴许他们之间的冲突把自己都搭了进去。你一想到亚历山大的情况就不寒而栗。

暗红骑士默认弃权。
深红斗篷的恶兽默认弃权。

如果均非上述情况：“我不想要暴力。”一位衣冠楚楚、身披红色的长者说道。“我相信面前的人能成为可靠的支援。”就在桌子对面，一个深红长袍下的身影隆隆道：“这就是你为什么这么弱。”它阴影中的面容转过来朝着你。你在昏暗的灯光中只能看到滴着涎水的可怕獠牙。“必须流血。”

暗红骑士投票“反对”。
深红斗篷的恶兽投票“赞成”。

抛硬币并如下更新剧本日志的钥匙部分：如果正面朝上，“暗红骑士”拥有法罗斯之光；如果背面朝上，“深红斗篷的恶兽”拥有法罗斯之光。

如果艾婕信任特别小组：艾婕上前一步，清清嗓子：“我曾经和基金会联络，因为藏在伊斯珀布尔的扭曲反棱镜有被第三方发现的危险。这些就是响应我的特工。他们没有将神器留下，而是选择交给我保管。我相信他们值得信赖，而且，不像我们中的某些人，还很有道德。”

艾婕·萨辛投票“反对”。

如果艾婕不信任特别小组：桌旁其他人看向艾婕，她垂下了眼睛。“我……”她结结巴巴，“我厌恶暴力，不像我们中的某些人一样乐在其中，因此拒绝参与这种事。”她若有所指，激怒了其中几位。但她渐渐抬起头，一脸的悲伤和坚毅，眼神对上了你。“但这些人不能相信，我也不能宽恕其罪过。”她静静地深呼吸：“我很抱歉。”

艾婕·萨辛弃权。

如果均非上述情况：“如果我们想要建立一个名正言顺的组织，”朱红头巾的女子礼貌地指出，“我们就不能见到挡路的就杀。我们的进步需要理解与合作。并且，我厌恶暴力。我们应该跟这些人合作，而非作对。”

艾婕·萨辛投票“反对”。

如果你和苋之间恩怨未了：苋露出病态的狞笑望着你：“噢，我等这一刻可真是太久了。”她拉长声音说着，眼里闪着光。“惹麻烦的蠢货，你难道以为自己干扰我们的计划还能不受惩罚？”

苋狂热地投票“赞成”。

如果情人重聚：苋和拉辛·法瑞保存完好的活尸彼此迷恋的对视实在叫人恶心，但他们间或还是睥睨你一眼。“你怎么想，最亲爱的拉辛？我们要不要饶了这些挡路的蠢货？”苋问道，“还是我们给他们上一课？”拉辛嘶哑地回道：“吾爱。没人能挡我们的路。把他除掉，以后也不会有人挡我们的路了。”

苋投票“赞成”。
拉辛·法瑞投票“赞成”。

如果苋离开同态会：“苋哪儿去了？”同志会里有人大声问道，众人的窃窃私语越来越大声。“她从不缺席会议。”你虽然被封了口，但还是笑了。至少艾琳最终可以摆脱同态会的控制，用自己的身份活下去。

苋默认弃权。

如果均非上述情况：接下来发言的是一个美丽的女子，她皮肤苍白，一身黑裙。她身上唯一的色彩就是头顶盛开的大花。“我们秘密行事自有原因，不是吗？”她样貌虽美，说话的语调音色却惹人厌恶。“这些人知道的太多了。杀了他们，就翻篇了。”

苋投票“赞成”。
苋拥有未绽之花，相应更新在剧本日志中。

如果你和索恩之间恩怨未了：索恩整了整自己长大衣下正装衬衫的袖口：“基金会阻碍我们的计划，不值得信任。我们应当消灭这个特别小组，继续谈收藏的事情。”索恩对上你的眼神，坚定如初，毫不动摇：“我警告过你别挡我们的路，嗯？”

索恩投票“赞成”。

如果特别小组与索恩达成交易：名为索恩之人向前一步：“我们海量的任务在全球各地都需要广泛合作。研究者、当局、罪犯。眼前这些也不例外。他们证明了自己派的上用场，在安克雷奇帮过我们；并且将钥匙交给我们妥善保管，也足见其智慧。”

索恩投票“反对”。

如果索恩消失：你惊讶地发现索恩居然也在人群中。可是你们上次见面的时候，索恩在安克雷奇北部完全消失。而现在，这人一言不发，绝口不提你们之间发生了什么。

索恩诡异地沉默着。

如果均非上述情况：下一位发言的人戴着红色长巾，铂金色头发，雪白的皮肤。“我跟眼前这些人没打过交道。”此人指着你说，“未能直接了解其能力，是否可靠也不曾检验，这样盲目投票实属不智。因此，我坐观其变。”

索恩弃权。
索恩拥有玄丧之镜，相应更新在剧本日志中。

如果艾里奇站在你这一边：艾里奇·佐尼·奥佩勒曲亚走出阴影，背上带鞘的剑金光闪闪，眼神十分缥缈。虽然无风，她红色的腰带却依然飘扬。她一如既往，用失落的韵文轻声低语。同志会有人翻译道：“奥佩勒曲亚声称……”译员惊讶地抬高了眉毛，“我们眼前之人确是大业的忠仆，亦如吾等。”你周围爆发出一阵窃窃私语。

艾里奇投票“反对”。

如果你和艾里奇之间恩怨未了：“别忘了奥佩勒曲亚的一票。”有个声音嘟囔道。“她在这儿？”另一人问道，“我们都试着联系她几周了。”聚集的同志会成员都转向房间的角落，你惊讶地发现幽灵般寂静的少女就在那里，远离众人。屋内寂静得诡异。要不是她的腰带还在一片寂静中缓缓飘动，你俨然已将她当作一尊雕像。

艾里奇诡异地沉默着。

如果均非上述情况：阴影里走出一个缥缈的身影。她一身白衣，背上带鞘的剑金光闪闪，乌黑的头发遮住了眼睛。虽然无风，她红色的腰带却依然飘扬。先是一声柔和颤动的哨音，接着她用一种你从没听过的语言开口。同志会里似乎有人能懂她的话，将这记作是对你的指控。

艾里奇投票“赞成”。
在结算下列任意选项前，如果德西欠你一笔：找出你之前放在安全位置的那张德西德柔·戴佳多·欧瓦瑞兹，查看另一面。然后，继续。

如果德西德柔·戴佳多·欧瓦瑞兹的另一面是剧情支援：突然一阵火光，是德西点亮了香烟。“这些家伙没问题。”他说，“现在可有更恶心的麻烦事呢。我在哈瓦那的时候，被那个你们知道是什么的鬼东西抓住了。是他们救了我——我还有什么可说的？所以，我挺他们。”

德西德柔·戴佳多·欧瓦瑞兹投票“反对”。

如果你和德西之间恩怨未了，或如果德西德柔·戴佳多·欧瓦瑞兹的另一面是遭遇卡牌牌背：你盯着德西，希望他能为你说话。但他只是点燃一根烟，望着你背后的墙壁。

德西德柔·戴佳多·欧瓦瑞兹诡异地沉默着。

如果均非上述情况：“我该知道这帮人他妈的是谁吗？”一个打着红领带的西装男点燃一根烟，长吐了一口。烟雾漂浮在黑暗的桌上。“浪费时间。难道你们一直都不知道要消除未知因素吗？把他们解决了，我们专心处理真正重要的事情吧。”

德西德柔·戴佳多·欧瓦瑞兹投票“赞成”。
德西德柔·戴佳多·欧瓦瑞兹拥有镜刃，相应更新在剧本日志中。

如果特别小组介入了阿巴冉的事务：突然，仪表堂堂、身材魁梧的阿巴冉·阿里戈利阿伽科一拳打在屋正中的仪式桌上。“这些入侵者！竟想毁了我！竟想夺走我的好运，我选中的宝物！”他气得发抖，脸涨红了，骨节发白。“我要亲自处罚入侵者！我要把他们分筋扒皮！我要——”他又吼了好一阵，怒火才消了点儿。

阿巴冉·阿里戈利阿伽科投票“赞成”。

如果并非上述情况：下一个说话的男人你并不认识。他仪表堂堂、身材魁梧，但更为夺目的，还是他右手食指上那颗巨大的红宝石。“时运眷顾，我们又一次得享巨福。”他洪亮的声音吸引了所有的注意。“现在我们的敌人就在面前受缚？为什么要拒绝这样一份大礼？要想继续我们的大业，怎能不好好盘问一番？兴许我们还能将其用作手段。是的，手段……”他的声音渐渐小了下去，唇边扬起邪恶的微笑。你恨不得他还是投票杀了你的好。

阿巴冉·阿里戈利阿伽科弃权。

无论如何：你看不见戴红手套男子的脸，但你能想象他恐怖的微笑。

戴红手套的男子诡异地沉默着。
如果特别小组了解了同志会的真相，立即跳转，不记录其余投票。
否则，如果有至少3位同志会成员诡异地沉默着，立即跳转，不记录其余投票。
如果均非上述情况，如常继续。

如果你和红衣女郎之间恩怨未了：你几乎没注意到藏在黑暗中的红衣女郎，她就站在另外两位同志会成员中间。她倾斜帽沿，盖过眼睛，脸上露出玩味的笑容。“这群人还说警察和探员一样，以为能对付我呢。”桌对面另一个戴着红眼镜的苍白男子站起来反驳她：“他们干涉了同志会的行动。”他吼道。“不。”女郎回道，“他们只是干涉了私人恩怨。要是你跟我有矛盾，红眼镜，冲我来，别冲他们。”

红衣女郎弃权。
血色监视者投票“赞成”。

如果你和血色监视者之间恩怨未了：突然，有一顶系着红带子的宽沿帽掉到了桌上，红衣女郎从阴影中现身。“基金会并不是我们最大的敌人，最大的敌人就在我们之中。这位特工身上可能并不戴红，但我保证他比我们里面一半人自称的都要正直。”桌对面，血色监视者用一块血红的布料擦了擦自己的红眼镜，露出的眼窝是一对骇人的空洞。“傻姑娘。”他的语气恶毒无比，“想最后再引人注目一次？”女郎怒视着他，抓着自己帽子中央，用劲之大，都抓皱了起来。“你们中有人知道这个恶心的杂种都干了什么吗？你们中真的有人在乎吗？”

红衣女郎投票“反对”。
血色监视者投票“赞成”。

如果血色监视者造成的苦难未止：红衣女郎从房间昏暗的角落里现身，她那顶熟悉的宽沿帽遮住了眼睛：“我在布宜诺斯艾利斯对付了自己人，那人的作为有碍我们的崇高利益。”她介绍道，“这些特工看到那里究竟发生了什么，还努力帮助了我。他们身上可能并不戴红，但我保证他们比我们里面一半人自称的都要正直。”人群中另一个声音问女郎她指的究竟是谁。“我们那位没有眼睛的‘朋友’。”她怒吼道，“我想他还在布宜诺斯艾利斯为害呢。但你们中真的有人在乎吗？”

Intro 1: You awaken in darkness. A sack is removed from your head and cast aside, and your cheek is squeezed and struck once or twice for good measure. “Wake up,” a sinister voice commands. You blink unconsciousness away and realize, with some panic, that you and your partners are bound to chairs. A gag prevents you from making any noise louder than a muffled cry.

As your eyes adjust to the dim light, you realize you must be underground. The large, windowless chamber is made of clean, worked stone, lit faintly by mercury vapor lamps. Scarlet tapestries line the walls, along with several glass cases and shelves containing old relics and historical artifacts. Dominating the room is an enormous central table, an elaborate pattern of lines and rings carved meticulously along its surface. Standing around this central table are a host of figures, some familiar to you, others unrecognizable. All of them bear red. Your heart surges in your throat. “You have been brought here to account for your crimes against the Coterie,” the voice states, “or to be commended, if that is the will of the Congress. We will now entertain any who wish to speak on your behalf, or against you.”

Proceed to The Trial 1.

Intro 2: You would never have found the secret hideout of the Red Coterie without the intel Commissioner Taylor sent you. The compound lies deep underground in the heart of Siberia, not far from the mysterious crater that marks the site of the notorious Tunguska event—a blast, or perhaps impact, the true nature of which has been shrouded in mystery for over a decade. Maybe there is a connection between this strange event and the Coterie’s presence—no, knowing the kind of dangerous artifacts the Coterie possesses, there is no doubt in your mind. The question is: which came first?

The compound’s entrance is masked by heavy snow and remote wilderness, but eventually, you find it—an unmarked steel door embedded in the side of a snowy hilltop, almost impossible to see from afar. You are surprised to find the door unlocked…but the moment you enter, you are set upon by Coterie guards with suspicious eyes and familiar red clothing. “We’ve been expecting you,” one of them says with a wicked grin. “Come. The Congress is about to begin.”

You have little choice but to follow. The guards lead you deeper and deeper into the complex, down steep, narrow stairways of worked stone and through dark, drab corridors, until finally you reach a large, windowless chamber lit faintly by mercury vapor lamps. Scarlet tapestries line the walls, along with several glass cases and shelves containing old relics and historical artifacts. Dominating the room is an enormous central table, an elaborate pattern of lines and rings carved meticulously along its surface. Standing around this central table are a host of figures, some familiar to you, others unrecognizable. All of them bear red. The door leading into the chamber slams shut behind you, and your heart surges in your throat. “Your timing is impeccable,” a voice among the gathered Coterie states. “We were just about to begin the vote.”

You inquire as to the nature of this vote, your mouth suddenly dry. You cannot shake the feeling that you have come here merely to look your own doom in the eyes. “A meeting has been called. To account for your crimes against the Coterie, or to be commended, if that is the will of the Congress. We will now entertain any who wish to speak on your behalf, or against you.” From behind, you are suddenly restrained and a gag is placed over your mouth. “Just a formality, I promise you,” the guard drawls with a grin.

Proceed to The Trial 1.

The Trial 2: With the voting complete, you are shoved to the floor. You struggle against your bonds, but are unable to free yourself, and vastly outnumbered, besides. There is no hope of escape. A cold blade is placed at the edge of your neck. “You who seek to harm our noble cause have been accused and charged with numerous crimes against the Coterie,” a voice states with dreadful gravity. The blade bites against your skin. A trail of blood trickles down your neck. “The punishment is death. May the crimson stain of your legacy be washed away.” You close your eyes and brace yourself.

Just then: a crash. Shouting and sounds of battle erupt throughout the room, a storm of clashing steel and gunfire. You are sent reeling as your would-be executioner is attacked by an unseen foe. You struggle again to free yourself, but are unable…until moments later, when you are dragged out of the chamber. Your bonds are cut, and you are brought to your feet by none other than the woman in the vermillion veil herself. Ece ushers you down the hall, whispering over the chaos of the battle. “We have to get out of here.” Several of the others who wear red follow in your wake, looking over their shoulders the entire time.

You ask what is going on as another rumble shudders throughout the halls. “The one with the red gloves, he…” she trails off, her hand trembling as she grips your arm. “He’s not what we thought he was. That man always creeped me out, but—to think—how could we have not known—?”

You ask her to start again, slower. “He attacked us,” she says, meeting your gaze as you duck into a quiet hall filled with scarlet tapestries. “The others fought him off, but…there was something strange about him. He was not human. It was something else entirely. It stole as many implements as it could and escaped, like…” she shudders. “…just like one of the creatures we seek to destroy.”

Thoughts run unbidden through your mind. If the man with the red gloves—or whatever it truly is—is after the remaining Keys, you have to stop it, at any cost. You pull away from Ece and begin marching back. “What are you doing?” she calls out. “The rest of them won’t show you any mercy, you know.” But your intentions are clear.

“If you’re going after that thing,” one of the others says to you, “then we’re coming, too.”

The Trial 3: Murmuring and debate erupt throughout the assembled Congress. The gag is taken out of your mouth, and your bindings are cut. With some reluctance, you are brought before the ceremonial table and given the chance to speak on your behalf. Your eyes seek out the members of the Coterie you know to be genuinely good, and as soon as the room is silent, you appeal to their sense of justice. For too long, the Red Coterie has allowed its members to wreak havoc and spread misery among the people simply to further their own ends. For too long, they have used their collected power not to guard humanity, but to plague it. As you speak, several of the people you have met nod amongst themselves. “They’re right,” the girl in the red coat announces, gesturing at several of the others who look on with sneers. “You all say you are motivated by a duty to humanity, yet you tolerate the presence of those who only do others harm. If this is the kind of organization you really are, I no longer wish to be a part of it.”

Ece nods along. “I agree. This is no longer a righteous organization.” She joins La Chica Roja’s side, along with several others. Among them is Desi, who simply tips the brim of his hat in your direction and slips you a subtle wink.

“Cleaning up the streets of scum has been my life’s work,” he declares, his eyes narrowing. “Maybe it’s time I start cleaning this place up, too.” A tense silence lingers in the chamber as the two sides stare one another down, but it’s clear that your side outnumbers the other. For a moment, you fear that the ensuing chaos will be impossible to survive.

Luckily, no such battle erupts. Seeing the wisdom in flight, your foes carefully filter out of the room, whispering, mumbling and hissing with vitriol. “You may wear red,” one of them spits, “but you will never be strong enough to stop what is coming without us. You are weak. You will be the doom of us all.”

Ece steps in front of the rest, shaking her head. “No. It is you who are weak. And by purging you from our ranks, we have only become stronger.”

• In your Campaign Log, record the cell overthrew the Red Coterie.

• Skip to The Trial 8.

The Trial 4: Murmuring and debate erupt throughout the assembled Congress. The gag is taken out of your mouth, and your bindings are cut. With some reluctance, you are brought before the ceremonial table and given the chance to speak on your behalf. Your eyes seek out the members of the Coterie who have seen your potential up close, and as soon as the room is silent, you appeal to their sense of logic and reason. You have been nothing but a valuable asset to the Red Coterie, and what’s more, you bring experience with the Foundation and the potential for both organizations to cooperate further. You seek the same goals as they do, and as your enemies from beyond gather to erase humanity from existence, only by working together can you stop this threat. As you speak, several of the people you have met nod in agreement. “They are, of course, correct,” Professor Masai speaks on your behalf. “We have let ourselves be motivated too long by petty desires while the threat of annihilation looms over us.”

Several of the others look on with disgust as more speak up. “We have inducted far worse into our ranks,” says the knight with many names. “These before us have proven themselves in more ways than one, and we need every ally we can get.”

“Agreed,” Thorne states, their voice level and calm as always. “I would call those on trial ‘trustworthy partners’ before I call them foes.” Their gaze meets yours, a meticulous smile hiding the vicious nature you know them to possess. Thorne would do anything to get what they want, and right now, what they want is you.

The members of the Coterie you have wronged shout and curse in bitter protest, but they are clearly outnumbered. A tense silence lingers in the chamber as the two sides stare one another down. For a moment, you fear it may even come to blows. “You may seek to wear red,” one of them spits, “but you will never be one of us.”

“If you no longer wish to be a part of this organization,” Professor Masai states, “You know where the door is.” Your detractors sit in hateful silence as the proceedings continue. The knight beckons you forward and inducts you into their order in a lengthy, solemn ritual. “With red we are bound,” he recites with gravitas, “through red we are one. Thus in red do we embrace our kin and our ken.” You are told to forsake your old life to take up a new one, for the betterment and guidance of all humanity. You think on your life, on the events that led you to this place, on those you hold dear and the many things you will leave behind. Then, you acquiesce.

The Trial 6: Before the next member is even given the chance to speak, a figure emerges from behind the man with the red gloves, and something small and dark is placed against the base of his skull. There is a thunder in your ears as the gunshot rings out across the chamber. The man’s face explodes not in grotesquerie, but in a flood of distorted mist that crests outward and reforms above the man’s hollowed body. It takes the vague shape of a many-armed spiral, like a galaxy of stars pinching all of reality around its otherworldly form. The clothes the Red-Gloved Man previously wore crumple to the ground, empty.

The rest of the assembled Coterie draw their weapons and attack the entity, but it quickly escapes the chamber, reassembling its ectoplasmic form before your very eyes on its way out. Several more of the things follow suit, the attire of their previous forms falling, limp and hollow, to the floor. From the shadows emerges the true figure of the Red-Gloved Man. “They are here,” he states with surprising nonchalance, reloading his sidearm. “Among us. Perhaps the rest of you might have noticed, had you kept your gaze on our mission.” He shares with you a knowing glance and the barest hint of an impish grin. “These ‘accused’ are to thank for my return to this realm. Without them, you might all be dead. This trial is over.” There is no debate whatsoever.

The gag is taken out of your mouth, and your bindings are cut. You are brought before the ceremonial table, standing by the man’s side. “What are they after? Where have you been?” one of the Coterie asks.

“They are after our world. Perhaps every world,” he replies, pulling his scarlet gloves taut around his hands. “But now is our chance to strike back. To follow them to their home and end this threat, once and for all.” Nods and murmurs of consent ripple throughout the assembly.

The Trial 7: Before the next member is even given the chance to speak, the Red-Gloved Man reaches out to grip their skull with uncanny strength, his arms lengthening into spindly wires of ectomatter. He crushes their skull inside the palm of his hands, staining his gloves a deeper crimson than ever before. The body slumps to the ground, and chaos ensues.

You watch in horror as more of the assembly begin to contort and reshape themselves, ambushing everyone around them in a macabre display. A storm of shouting, clashing steel, and gunfire erupts throughout the room. Each slain member of the Congress is erased in their entirety. You are sent reeling as your captors, too, are expunged from reality. You crawl along the ground as the fray rages on, eventually finding a shard of glass upon which to cut your bonds. By the time you free your companions and rise to your feet, the entities have fled. The last thing you see is the shapeless elongated remnants of the Red-Gloved Man escaping out the door you came from.

You survey the damage, but surprisingly, there isn’t much to look at. Save for you and a few articles of discarded and forgotten red attire, the chamber is completely empty.

To your horror, you recall none of their names or monikers. Not a single one.

• In your Campaign Log, record the Red Coterie was destroyed from within.

The Trial 8: With the trial proceedings over, the Congress finally reaches other affairs. “There is still the matter of the Outsiders,” one among them states. “We have assembled our strength in order to prepare for the inevitable, but how can we be certain our dimension is of any interest to them? We cannot seek to understand such abstruse entities.”

You chime in, telling the Congress of everything you have seen during your travels and your operations with the Foundation: the strange happenings across the globe have only grown in frequency, and you have reason to believe they are intelligent and malicious—not mindless and incomprehensible. What’s worse, they appear to be after the very same keys as everyone else.

“If they are stirring, preparing for war,” another member declares, “then we must do the same. We have among our assembly bearers of the most powerful artufacts this order has uncovered. Let us put them to good use and exterminate this threat once and for all.” Nods and murmurs of consent ripple throughout the assembly.

“But if they are intelligent entities as our new friends claim they are, how could they possibly know so much of our inner workings?” Your detractor argues. A dreadful hunch stirs in your mind. You scan the room and remark that one among the Congress is missing. The rest of the assembly follows your gaze, with several of them standing to search the chamber more thoroughly. One of them confirms your suspicions by raising a single red glove, discarded and forgotten as though mundane, immaterial.

The woman in the vermillion veil is the first to understand your thread of logic. “Spread out,” she shouts, her voice warbling. “Find him. Learn where he is headed. And be ready for anything.”

It doesn’t take long before the doorway is found—a shimmering portal of extradimensional energy, ebbing with eldritch power. “It’s closing,” one of the others observes. Indeed, the doorway seems to be shrinking as it steadily swirls, and soon enough there will be nothing left of it. “We don’t have much time.”
